features.scope: GET /v2/query?verify=true transcribes bounded sums, products, and rational scaling over supported sin/cos/tan calls at rational multiples of pi into the exact CAG route; after Lean checks the composed theorem, the Result pod displays the same exact value used by the proof. Division is limited to nonzero rational denominators and powers to nonnegative integer exponents through 16

POST /api/cag/v1/WolframLanguageCompute and /v2/query verify exact Tan values by composing Lean-checked Sin and Cos values where the corresponding cosine is nonzero; rational-pi period, reflection, and half-pi-complement reductions are preserved; results are returned as exact sine/cosine quotients and tangent poles remain unsupported

typed bounded integer/real polynomial arithmetic and formula-text route /v1/prove-formula; supports addition, subtraction, multiplication, division by nonzero numeric constants, and powers up to 16 (maximum degree 32); nonlinear Lean checking uses nlinarith when supported and depends on local Mathlib setup
safe bounded polynomial comparison parser; variables require explicit Int/Real sorts; not natural-language formalization

Z3 polynomial witness independently replayed against the submitted AST with exact integer/rational arithmetic; algebraic irrational real models return unknown unless an exact rational witness is available

SymPy 1.14; bounded safe expression grammar; validate, simplify, factor, expand, finite numeric evaluation, differentiate, integrate, two-sided real limits, Taylor series through order 32, finite integer sum/product with empty-range identities, explicit bounded one-variable plots with inline SVG output and configurable width, solve, identity, and common trig, hyperbolic, and inverse-hyperbolic functions including sec/csc/cot, asinh, acosh, tanh, coth, sech, and csch; named_units bind a curated set of common length, time, mass, volume, angle, and derived SI units and rejects incompatible dimensions in additions; outputs are not formal proofs
native expressions plus bounded presentation LaTeX and presentation MathML normalization; unsupported constructs are rejected; no arbitrary TeX or Content MathML

SymbolicRequest operation numeric and GET /v2/query N[expression] or N[expression, precision] evaluate bounded finite numeric expressions without free symbols; default precision is 16 digits and explicit integer precision is 1-500; uses SymPy and returns an approximation without Lean proof evidence; decimal input literals retain exact base-10 semantics

typed, versioned assumptions for AngleUnit, LogBase, Unit, DateOrder, MixedFraction, ListOrTimes, ListOrNumber, NumberBase, I, TimeAMOrPM, and Function; bare numeric sin/cos/tan, parenthesized log calls, and whitespace log-number calls in compound formulas; standalone number m resolves meter, US minim, or minute; valid slash-separated M/D/YYYY or D/M/YYYY dates expose both orders when both are valid; positive whole-plus-proper-fraction input resolves as a mixed fraction or product; numeric symbol pairs resolve as multiplication or a two-item list; a thousands-grouped numeric comma resolves as a number or list; standalone 8–64 digit binary-looking strings resolve as base 2 or 10; lowercase i resolves as imaginary or variable; ambiguous 1-12 hour clock values resolve as AM or PM using the server-local meridiem default; caller overrides by type and one-based per-occurrence overrides using assumption_id@N for AngleUnit, parenthesized LogBase, and unparenthesized Function log calls; Function and LogBase remain independent when both syntax forms occur; unselected calls retain service defaults; query-wide and per-occurrence choices cannot be mixed for one assumption type; rankings do not select assumptions; project-specific route is /v1/interpret
deterministic baseline included; optional Decima ranking; classifier scores are not calibrated for this service and do not establish truth

generic GDP data requests expose versioned nominal and PPP alternatives without a default; /v2/validatequery returns the unresolved GDPType choice and /v2/query accepts an explicit gdp:type:nominal or gdp:type:ppp override; the choice selects a typed Wikidata property and is included in the result

generic GDP per capita requests expose versioned nominal and PPP alternatives without a default; /v2/validatequery returns the unresolved GDPPerCapitaType choice and /v2/query accepts an explicit gdp-per-capita:type:nominal or gdp-per-capita:type:ppp override; the choice selects a typed Wikidata property and is included in the result
Wikidata, DBnomics, NIST CODATA subset, GeoNames, Open-Meteo; provenance returned

POST /api/cag/v1/WolframLanguageCompute supports TrigExpand for bounded sums/differences of variable arguments and integer multiples 2 through 12 of one variable in Sin and Cos; SymPy proposes the expansion and Lean proves the identity over the reals; other trig functions and angle multipliers above 12 remain unsupported

POST /api/cag/v1/WolframLanguageCompute accepts rational Pi multiples with integer numerator and denominator up to 256 bits when nearest-integer period reduction leaves a base angle of zero or Pi/d for supported d; Sin/Cos also accept Pi/2-Pi/d for d=5,8,10,16,32, powers of two through 4096, and up to eight successive halvings from Pi/6 or Pi/10. Sin/Cos support d=2,3,4,5,6,8,10,16,32, powers of two from 64 through 4096, and d=6*2^k or 10*2^k for 1<=k<=8; Tan supports d=3,4,6 and rejects poles. Lean checks period, reflection, and cofunction identities; fifth/tenth values derive from Mathlib's cosine-at-Pi/5 theorem and dyadic/iterated half-angle values from Mathlib half-angle theorems. The queryresult returns the documented timing, parsetiming, and parsetimedout fields; the referenced contract does not define separate scan/format duration fields. Other reduced angles and arbitrary numeric angles remain unsupported

Definite Integrate[Sin[a*x+b*Pi],{x,l,u}] and Integrate[Cos[a*x+b*Pi],{x,l,u}] support rational nonzero a and rational Pi phase offset b, with bounds in {-Pi,-Pi/2,-Pi/4,-Pi/8,-Pi/16,-Pi/32,0,Pi/32,Pi/16,Pi/8,Pi/4,Pi/2,Pi} and scaled, shifted endpoint angles in {-2Pi,-Pi,-Pi/2,-Pi/4,-Pi/8,-Pi/16,-Pi/32,0,Pi/32,Pi/16,Pi/8,Pi/4,Pi/2,Pi,2Pi}; SymPy proposes exact values in the Q-span of 1, sqrt(2), sqrt(2+sqrt(2)), sqrt(2-sqrt(2)), sqrt(2+sqrt(2+sqrt(2))), sqrt(2-sqrt(2+sqrt(2))), sqrt(2+sqrt(2+sqrt(2+sqrt(2)))), and sqrt(2-sqrt(2+sqrt(2+sqrt(2)))); Lean checks the affine phase, interval fundamental theorem, and endpoint identities; other real-radian offsets and non-affine or non-Sin/Cos trigonometric integrands remain unsupported

DBnomics full-text dataset search returns ranked dataset candidates with provider/dataset codes and source links; GET /v2/query accepts 'series search: <phrase>' or 'dbnomics search: <phrase>'; callers select a dataset before searching its series

POST /v1/knowledge/query and GET /v2/query support full-text series discovery inside a selected DBnomics provider/dataset via GET /v22/series/{provider}/{dataset}?q=...; GET /v2/query accepts seriesoffset (0-10000) and returns five candidates per page; POST uses offset; results preserve series code, name, dimensions, index time, source link, total count, limit, and offset; selection remains with the caller before observations are fetched

POST /v1/knowledge/query accepts Wikidata population; GET /v2/query routes 'population of <entity>' and related forms to P1082 retrieval; up to three ranked entity matches are preserved, preferred or latest dated statements are returned with ties, and source data is not presented as a Lean proof

POST /v1/knowledge/query accepts allowlisted Wikidata nominal GDP P2131 and GDP at purchasing power parity P4010 properties; GET /v2/query supports explicit nominal/PPP requests and exposes generic GDP as a GDPType clarification with stable caller-selectable IDs; quantities preserve currency/unit, bounds, rank, references, and point-in-time qualifiers, choosing preferred or latest dated statements with ties; retrieved values are source data, not Lean proofs

POST /v1/knowledge/query accepts allowlisted nominal GDP per capita P2132 and PPP GDP per capita P2299 properties; GET /v2/query accepts explicit measure phrases and returns a GDPPerCapitaType clarification for ambiguous 'GDP per capita of <entity>'; quantities preserve currency/unit, bounds, rank, references, and point-in-time qualifiers; retrieved values are source data, not Lean proofs

POST /v1/knowledge/query accepts the allowlisted Wikidata P36 property; GET /v2/query routes 'capital of <entity>' and possessive forms to capital relationships; up to three ranked entity matches and non-deprecated relationship statements are preserved with time qualifiers, and source data is not presented as a Lean proof

POST /v1/knowledge/query accepts allowlisted Wikidata country P17 and continent P30 relationships; GET /v2/query routes 'country of <entity>', 'what country is <entity> in', 'continent of <entity>', and 'what continent is <entity> in'; up to three ranked entity candidates are retained, non-deprecated relationship statements preserve references, rank, qualifiers, and multi-valued continents, and P17 is not intended for people; results are retrieved data, not Lean proofs

POST /v1/knowledge/query accepts allowlisted Wikidata P37 official language and P38 currency; GET /v2/query routes official-language and currency intents through these properties; up to three ranked entity candidates are preserved with claim rank, qualifiers, and references where available; bounded process-local response cache; results are retrieved source data, not Lean proofs

local endpoint; exact rational arithmetic with exact base-10 decimal tokens and bounded polynomial Simplify/Expand/Factor; D[expression, variable] supports polynomial and selected real functions including ArcSinh, ArcCosh, ArcTanh with strict interval conditions, Tanh, and Log on positive arguments, Tan where Cos[argument] is nonzero, and Sec/Csc/Cot via Lean-checked reciprocal-trig identities with explicit nonzero cosine or sine conditions; variable denominators use explicit conditions returned in evidence.domain_conditions; Lean-checked HasDerivAt proofs; indefinite Integrate[expression, variable] supports selected variable-denominator, logarithmic, tangent, reciprocal-trigonometric, inverse-trigonometric, and inverse-hyperbolic antiderivatives, including Sec[x]^2, Csc[x]^2, and Cot[x]^2 cases only after Lean checks their HasDerivAt certificate and returns required nonzero, positive, strict inverse-trig, or inverse-hyperbolic domain conditions, including Integrate[1/Sqrt[1-x^2], x], Integrate[ArcSin[x], x], Integrate[ArcCos[x], x], scaled inverse-trig arguments, Integrate[1/Sqrt[1+x^2], x], and Integrate[ArcSinh[x], x], Integrate[1/Sqrt[x^2-1], x], and Integrate[ArcCosh[x], x]; definite integration accepts exact rational bounds and selected exact Pi-multiple bounds for rational-frequency Sin[a*x+b*Pi] and Cos[a*x+b*Pi] with rational Pi phase offsets, including ±Pi/4, ±Pi/8, ±Pi/16, and ±Pi/32 bounds with Lean-checked nested-radical values; Lean proves affine nonzero conditions implied by exact interval bounds and reports unresolved conditions in evidence.domain_conditions; verified examples include 1/x and 1/(x+1) on [1,2] with no returned conditions, 1/(x-a) on [0,1] with an explicit interval condition, and 1/Sqrt[1-x^2] on [0,1/2] returning pi/6 with a checked inverse-trig endpoint identity while retaining the square-root nonzero condition; calculus grammar bounds powers 0-16, 256-bit numeric components, 256 nodes, and 32 levels; non-elementary antiderivatives remain unsupported; free symbols are real parameters; bounded finite Sum/Product supports inclusive integer ranges up to 128 terms for rational-polynomial inputs, including negative and empty ranges, with Lean proofs and finite rational-function limits at exact rational or bounded rational-polynomial points in real parameters (degree up to 64, coefficient components up to 256 bits), with free real parameters and explicit denominator conditions returned in evidence, plus selected removable singularities with explicit products and SymPy-proposed factors of denominator polynomial components with degree at most 16 at exact rational and symbolic polynomial points, subject to expression and coefficient bounds and Lean factorization proofs and explicit nonzero-at-point conditions for other factors; the exact Sin[Pi] special case and bounded additive and integer-multiple TrigExpand through 12x; each result is compiled by Lean and axiom-audited

GET /v2/query width controls text-oriented SVGs and maxwidth controls structural mathematical SVGs; both default to 500 and accept 100–1600; mag scales content in structural mathematical SVGs from 0.5 to 2.0 without changing pod dimensions; plotwidth remains separate; provider and plot images do not apply mag

POST /v1/natural-language/prove uses a configured Kimina-compatible OpenAI chat-completions endpoint to generate one Lean theorem from natural language; the first request returns a sanitized, reviewable Lean draft and a statement digest without running Lean; the caller must submit the matching draft ID and digest with approve_formalization=true before Lean compiles and audits the theorem; drafts are process-local, expire after 15 minutes, and are capped at 128 per process; one proof repair attempt is allowed only if the theorem signature remains unchanged; caller approval and Lean checking do not establish natural-language semantic fidelity

local /v2/query JSON/XML queryresult envelope, native and bounded presentation LaTeX/MathML symbolic input, explicit numeric N[expression] evaluation plus simplify/factor/expand/differentiate/integrate/limit/series/plot/sum/product/solve/identity operations plus bounded deterministic natural-language templates for evaluate, simplify, factor, expand, differentiate, integrate, solve, limit, series, integer-bounded finite sums/products, and plot; ambiguous function scope requires explicit parentheses; natural-language query results remain SymPy computations unless verify=true requests bounded Lean evidence; solve proofs cover supported real polynomial roots only when the SymPy solution set exactly matches the Lean candidate; proofs cover the selected formula and not English fidelity; default plaintext,image format, inline SVG images for mathematical Input/Result/DecimalApproximation and provider Input/result subpods (formula images structurally render a bounded presentation-MathML subset with escaped-text fallback; current-weather and other provider images render escaped plaintext; plots use sampled graphs and plotwidth 100–1600, default 200; text-oriented SVGs use width 100–1600, default 500; seven-day Open-Meteo weather forecast charts are implemented and use plotwidth; other provider-specific charts/maps remain unavailable), ignorecase query control, AngleUnit/LogBase/Function assumptions, standalone quantity Unit alternatives for number m, typed quantities for curated common physical-unit literals, DateOrder alternatives for valid ambiguous numeric dates, MixedFraction alternatives for a positive whole number followed by a proper fraction, ListOrTimes alternatives for a numeric literal and spaced single-letter symbol, ListOrNumber alternatives for one correctly grouped thousands comma, NumberBase alternatives for standalone binary-looking integers, I alternatives for lowercase i, TimeAMOrPM alternatives for ambiguous clock values, Function alternatives for unparenthesized log input, numeric approximation pods with repeatable More/Fewer digit states, plaintext/MathML/MInput/MOutput including unit quantities, dates, and list values, pod selectors, isolated SymPy parsetimeout for mathematical inputs, per-pod formatting budget checked after bounded output rendering, totaltimeout deadline spanning symbolic execution, provider retrieval, and pod rendering; final XML/JSON serialization occurs afterward, bounded in-process async delivery for one primary pod, optional /v2/query verify=true with separate prooftimeout and inspectable Lean source/axiom audit for supported polynomial, real-calculus, and finite polynomial Sum/Product computations over inclusive integer ranges of up to 128 terms and rational-function limits at exact rational or bounded rational-polynomial points in real parameters with free real parameters and explicit denominator conditions returned in evidence, plus selected product-factor removable singularities with affine vanishing factors, including expanded denominator polynomial components of degree at most 16 factored by SymPy subject to expression and coefficient bounds and Lean verification, and explicit nonzero-at-point conditions for remaining factors, /v2/validatequery, plus source-backed current weather and seven-day Open-Meteo forecasts with location/units and a daily chart, CODATA, Wikidata, GeoNames, and DBnomics pods; general Wolfram-style typesetting remains unavailable; podtimeout and formattimeout are checked after bounded render operations and do not interrupt an active renderer; no Wolfram AppID or remote Wolfram calls

WolframLanguageCompute exact rational arithmetic, bounded polynomial Simplify/Expand/Factor, Lean-checked polynomial and Sin/Cos/Tan/Sec/Csc/Cot/ArcTan/ArcSinh/ArcCosh/ArcTanh/Tanh/Coth/Sech/Csch/Exp/Sinh/Cosh/Log derivatives with explicit reciprocal-trig, inverse-hyperbolic, Coth and Csch pole conditions, selected variable-denominator, logarithmic, tangent, hyperbolic-tangent, hyperbolic-cotangent, reciprocal-trigonometric, inverse-trigonometric, and inverse-hyperbolic antiderivatives with explicit domain conditions, definite supported-expression integrals with exact rational bounds plus rational-frequency Sin/Cos cases with rational Pi phase offsets at selected Pi-multiple bounds, including scaled endpoint angles through ±2Pi; partial Full Results-style protocol; broad natural-language coverage, most render formats, provider domains, independently formatted multi-pod async delivery, other pod-state families, and full parameter compatibility remain unimplemented

POST /api/cag/v1/WolframLanguageCompute requires code and accepts line (default 1), maxChars (default 10000), and timeConstraint (default 60); response includes result, code, success, and uuid; evaluation timeouts return HTTP 200 with the documented message-bearing EvaluationTimeExceeded Failure and success=true; accepts configured key directly or as Bearer token

D[ArcTan[f(x)],x] supports bounded expressions in the real calculus grammar; indefinite Integrate supports ArcTan[x] and 1/(1+x^2) when Lean checks the resulting HasDerivAt proof; any generated domain conditions are returned in evidence

Lean-checked ArcSin and ArcCos derivatives for bounded real expressions with explicit strict argument bounds -1 < argument < 1; out-of-range constant inputs are rejected rather than treated as real-valued

Lean-checked ArcSinh, ArcCosh, and ArcTanh derivatives; indefinite integrals for 1/Sqrt[1+x^2], ArcSinh[x], 1/Sqrt[x^2-1], ArcCosh[x], and 1/(1-x^2); ArcCosh requires argument > 1 and ArcTanh requires -1 < argument < 1; generated positivity and denominator conditions are reported in evidence.domain_conditions

Lean-checked Tanh derivatives for bounded real compositions and indefinite Integrate[Tanh[x],x] when SymPy proposes log(cosh(x)); the proof derives cosh nonzero from positivity, so no false domain condition is returned

Definite Integrate[Tanh[a*x+b],{x,l,u}] supports rational nonzero slopes and exact rational bounds; Lean checks the log-cosh endpoint difference through the interval fundamental theorem; cosh positivity means no domain conditions are needed

Lean-checked Coth derivatives for bounded real compositions with explicit Sinh[argument] != 0 pole conditions; indefinite Integrate[Coth[a*x+b],x] for rational nonzero a returns log(Abs[Sinh[a*x+b]])/a when Lean checks the HasDerivAt certificate; generated domain conditions are returned in evidence.domain_conditions

Lean-checked Sech and Csch derivatives for bounded real compositions; Sech uses Real.cosh positivity to prove its denominator nonzero without exposing a condition, while Csch returns the explicit Sinh[argument] != 0 pole condition

Indefinite Integrate[Sech[a*x+b],x] supports rational nonzero slopes a and affine real arguments; it returns ArcTan[Sinh[a*x+b]]/a only after Lean checks the derivative using cosh^2-sinh^2=1; no extra domain condition is needed

Definite Integrate[Sech[a*x+b],{x,l,u}] supports rational nonzero slopes and exact rational bounds; Lean checks the arctan-sinh endpoint difference through the interval fundamental theorem; no domain conditions are needed because cosh is positive

Indefinite Integrate[Csch[a*x+b],x] supports affine real arguments with rational nonzero slopes a; it returns Log[Abs[Tanh[(a*x+b)/2]]]/a only after Lean checks the derivative using the hyperbolic double-angle identity, with explicit nonzero tanh-half-argument and sinh-argument conditions; nonlinear Csch arguments remain unsupported

Definite Integrate[Csch[a*x+b],{x,l,u}] supports rational nonzero slopes and exact rational bounds when the affine argument has the same nonzero sign at both endpoints; Lean proves the endpoint log-tanh difference through the interval fundamental theorem and returns interval-wide sinh and tanh-half-argument nonzero conditions; intervals containing or crossing the Csch pole are rejected

Definite Integrate[Coth[a*x+b],{x,l,u}] supports rational nonzero slopes and exact rational bounds when the affine argument has the same nonzero sign at both endpoints; Lean checks the endpoint log-sinh difference through the interval fundamental theorem and returns an interval-wide sinh nonzero condition; intervals containing or crossing the Coth pole are rejected
Lean-checked Sqrt derivatives require a positive variable argument; selected antiderivatives such as Integrate[1/Sqrt[x],x] return explicit positivity and denominator conditions

D[Log[base,argument],variable] and selected indefinite and definite Integrate cases support statically rational bases greater than zero and different from one; Lean proves the base logarithm is nonzero; definite integration requires an affine real argument that stays positive over exact rational bounds, and Lean checks the final result; variable bases and nonlinear definite arguments remain unsupported

POST /api/cag/v1/WolframLanguageCompute accepts univariate rational-coefficient polynomials through degree eight when they factor completely over the rationals; degree-five through degree-eight coefficient components are limited to 128 bits. Exact real quadratic-radical roots, no-real-root quadratics, and nonzero constant equations remain supported. Rational linear systems with one to four equations and two to four variables produce unique solutions, parametric rules for consistent underdetermined systems, or empty solution sets. Lean checks each returned solution set against the equation or system. Nonlinear systems, systems with more than four equations or variables, complex-domain solving, degree above eight, degree-three through degree-eight polynomials without complete rational factorization, and higher-degree inputs exceeding the coefficient bound remain unsupported

GET /v2/query accepts scantimeout (default 3 seconds, range 0.1-30) as a distinct budget for symbolic computation or provider retrieval before output formatting; timed-out responses identify the scan stage; partial scanner fan-out is not implemented

GET /v2/query accepts podtimeout (default 4 seconds) per output pod and formattimeout (default 8 seconds) cumulatively, each in range 0.1-30 seconds; current bounded synchronous renderers are checked after completion and an over-budget pod is omitted, but an active renderer is not interrupted

Scan timeout responses may include a single-use opaque continuation URL; /v2/recalculate/{job_id} reruns the saved single-result request with increased scan and total budgets, returns new result pods without Input, warnings, or assumptions, and can issue a further token while budgets can increase; process-local token storage is bounded to 256 retained jobs and 4 active continuations with 30-minute expiry; no solver state or completed scanner work is reused

GET /v2/query async responses provide a primary-pod async URL and a query-level asyncquery URL; /v2/asyncQuery/{job_id} returns the complete queryresult envelope from the same computation, while /v2/asyncPod/{job_id} returns the primary pod; polling either URL leaves the other available until the in-process 30-minute expiry; one query is computed once, but pods are not delivered progressively and partial scanner fan-out is not implemented

GET /v2/query supports format=cell for mathematical Input, Result, and DecimalApproximation subpods and provider input/result subpods; returns a safe text-backed Wolfram Cell[BoxData[FormBox[RowBox[…]]]] wrapper, not rich Wolfram notebook typesetting

Wikidata properties P2046 area and P2044 elevation above sea level are available from POST /v1/knowledge/query and GET /v2/query phrases such as 'land area of France', 'elevation of Mount Everest', and 'altitude of Mount Everest'; property data preserves candidate ranking, units, bounds, statement rank, reference counts, and bounded qualifier details; measurements are retrieved source data, not Lean proofs

Wikidata P625 coordinate location is available from POST /v1/knowledge/query and GET /v2/query phrases such as 'coordinates of Paris' and 'GPS coordinates for Paris'; ranked entity candidates retain validated latitude/longitude, globe, precision, statement rank, reference counts, statement ID, and bounded qualifiers; coordinates are retrieved source data, not Lean proofs
no contract fixtures have been run

POST /api/cag/v1/WolframLanguageCompute accepts N[expression] and N[expression, precision] for exact rational expressions, square roots of nonnegative rationals, exact Sin/Cos/Tan values reducible to rational linear combinations or positive-denominator quotients of supported nested square roots at 1-500 significant digits, and bounded Pi expressions involving rational arithmetic, square roots, sign-definite products, nonnegative integer powers up to 16 with sign-definite bases (including negative bases), and quotients with sign-definite denominator intervals when the available Mathlib interval proves the requested error; affine Pi expressions allow up to 100 significant digits; other interval-evaluated Pi expressions are capped at 100 digits and accepted only when interval analysis proves the requested error; defaults to 16; Lean proves an absolute-error bound for evidence.numeric_approximation.value using exact trig composition, recursive rational interval bounds for roots and other bounded expressions, Mathlib built-in pi_gt_d20/pi_lt_d20 bounds through 20 digits and generated rational bounds proved by Mathlib pi_lower_bound/pi_upper_bound tactics above 20 digits, and norm_num for rational results; products are declined when factor intervals do not establish their signs, nonzero powers are declined when base intervals cross zero, and quotients are declined when denominator intervals cross zero; near-cancellation and large Pi coefficients may be rejected at high precision; other algebraic/transcendental inputs remain unsupported by this certified path
